plan: A whimsical, high-contrast arcade-style swamp level structured as a winding channel bounded by high, root-tangled mud cliffs that contain the play area. The level progresses from a safe, low-lying muddy bank cluttered with hollow logs and overgrown cattails, across a wide, hazard-filled river channel populated by organic stepping stones—including giant mossy lily pads, drifting logs, and partially submerged ancient stone pillars—and culminates at a grand, elevated frog-toad shrine carved directly into a colossal, hollowed-out cypress stump. Throughout the waterway, glowing lotus blossoms and lantern-capped reeds trace a winding path of progression, while ruins and massive swamp flora define the boundaries, ensuring a strong sense of verticality and clear navigation towards the final temple goal.

plan: The starting bank is structured as a wide, safe staging area positioned within the surrounding U-shaped root walls. A flat, elevated central starting pad made of packed, dry mud provides a clear player departure point. Facing toward the open water, the area features several physical obstacles including horizontal mossy hollow logs of different sizes; some are oriented parallel to the shore to act as low jumping barriers, while one large hollow log tunnel runs perpendicular, pointing directly toward the first river crossing ahead. Flanking the side walls of the bank are dense clusters of thick, oversized cattails and leafy reeds rooted in shallow mud. Along the forward water edge, a series of flat mossy stones and half-buried wooden planks are arranged as level launching pads to guide progression and offer safe vantage points for navigating into the river.

plan: A wide aquatic crossing structured across the center water floor, forming a clear progression pathway between the muddy bank and the shrine foundation. The crossing is organized into three distinct, spaced-out traversal bands aligning with the water channel. The first band, nearest to the start bank, consists of multiple wide, flat, circular mossy lily pads floating on the surface. The middle band features long, ancient wood logs aligned horizontally to bridge the center gap. The final band, closest to the shrine cliff, is composed of several tall and thick vertical stone pillars with flat carved tops that protrude above the water level, offering solid, elevated stepping locations. This tiered arrangement of platforms forms multiple non-linear crossing routes from left to right across the hazardous waterway.

plan: An elevated, circular sanctuary situated within and immediately around a colossal hollow cypress stump. The area features an outer semi-circular wooden ceremonial terrace that projects forward from the stump's base to serve as the landing platform. A wide, arched portal carved into the gnarled trunk wall leads into the circular inner hollow of the stump. Within this hollowed core, the floor transition to flat, ancient stone tiles that encircle a raised stone dais positioned against the back wall. This central dais holds a large, moss-covered stone frog deity statue. The interior wood walls of the hollow trunk rise upward to an open-air top, with shallow stone drainage runnels and low stone offering bowls lining the perimeter of the chamber floor.

plan: An elevated, circular sanctuary situated within and immediately around a colossal hollow cypress stump. The area features an outer semi-circular wooden ceremonial terrace that projects forward from the stump's base to serve as the landing platform. A wide, arched portal carved into the gnarled trunk wall leads into the circular inner hollow of the stump. Within this hollowed core, the floor transition to flat, ancient stone tiles that encircle a raised stone dais positioned against the back wall. This central dais holds a large, moss-covered stone frog deity statue. The interior wood walls of the hollow trunk rise upward to an open-air top, with shallow stone drainage runnels and low stone offering bowls lining the perimeter of the chamber floor.

plan: A whimsical, high-contrast arcade-style swamp level structured as a winding channel bounded by high, root-tangled mud cliffs that contain the play area. The level progresses from a safe, low-lying muddy bank cluttered with hollow logs and overgrown cattails, across a wide, hazard-filled river channel populated by organic stepping stones—including giant mossy lily pads, drifting logs, and partially submerged ancient stone pillars—and culminates at a grand, elevated frog-toad shrine carved directly into a colossal, hollowed-out cypress stump. Throughout the waterway, glowing lotus blossoms and lantern-capped reeds trace a winding path of progression, while ruins and massive swamp flora define the boundaries, ensuring a strong sense of verticality and clear navigation towards the final temple goal.

prompt: A swamp with islands, designed as a top-down arcade level where a frog can jump from island to island

A grand, elevated temple area carved into a colossal hollowed-out cypress stump, acting as the ultimate reward and destination atop high mud ruins.

plan: The starting bank is structured as a wide, safe staging area positioned within the surrounding U-shaped root walls. A flat, elevated central starting pad made of packed, dry mud provides a clear player departure point. Facing toward the open water, the area features several physical obstacles including horizontal mossy hollow logs of different sizes; some are oriented parallel to the shore to act as low jumping barriers, while one large hollow log tunnel runs perpendicular, pointing directly toward the first river crossing ahead. Flanking the side walls of the bank are dense clusters of thick, oversized cattails and leafy reeds rooted in shallow mud. Along the forward water edge, a series of flat mossy stones and half-buried wooden planks are arranged as level launching pads to guide progression and offer safe vantage points for navigating into the river.

plan: A wide aquatic crossing structured across the center water floor, forming a clear progression pathway between the muddy bank and the shrine foundation. The crossing is organized into three distinct, spaced-out traversal bands aligning with the water channel. The first band, nearest to the start bank, consists of multiple wide, flat, circular mossy lily pads floating on the surface. The middle band features long, ancient wood logs aligned horizontally to bridge the center gap. The final band, closest to the shrine cliff, is composed of several tall and thick vertical stone pillars with flat carved tops that protrude above the water level, offering solid, elevated stepping locations. This tiered arrangement of platforms forms multiple non-linear crossing routes from left to right across the hazardous waterway.

plan: An elevated, circular sanctuary situated within and immediately around a colossal hollow cypress stump. The area features an outer semi-circular wooden ceremonial terrace that projects forward from the stump's base to serve as the landing platform. A wide, arched portal carved into the gnarled trunk wall leads into the circular inner hollow of the stump. Within this hollowed core, the floor transition to flat, ancient stone tiles that encircle a raised stone dais positioned against the back wall. This central dais holds a large, moss-covered stone frog deity statue. The interior wood walls of the hollow trunk rise upward to an open-air top, with shallow stone drainage runnels and low stone offering bowls lining the perimeter of the chamber floor.
